exact.квитанция с главной почты: a receipt from the main post office
exact.Вот квитанция с главной почты, за телегр: Here's a receipt from the main post office, for a telegram. Who I sent it to, I couldn't tell you now, but I keep the receipt, it's got such a lovely stamp on it.
exact.В Сараеве перемены шли по долине: город: In Sarajevo change came along the valley: the city kept stretching further west along the river, buses and then trolleybuses joined the tram, and a cable car went up Trebević. Each time we had to work out all over again where the relatives lived now and how to get to them.
exact.Как-то летом мы с подругой пошли гулять: One summer my friend and I went for a walk along the Miljacka and argued about which bridge was the prettiest. We argued until dark and never settled it, and then went home over a third one that neither of us had even thought of.
exact.Меня взяли кондукторшей на трамвай. Перв: They took me on as a conductor on the tram. The first week I mixed up the stops and called them out so confidently that passengers got off at the wrong place and didn't argue.
exact.Я знала, кто из постоянных садится всегд: I knew which regulars always sat in the very same seat, and if the seat was taken I had to sort it out like a family quarrel.
exact.На пенсию я ушла с трамвая. На остановке: I retired from the tram. At a stop I still automatically work out how many people will squeeze into the carriage.
exact.До пенсии на трамвае я не доработала: в: I didn't make it to my pension on the tram: in May of ninety-two the tram stopped. I never handed in my conductor's bag, it hangs in my hallway.
exact.телеграфистка на главной почте: a telegraphist at the main post office
exact.После курсов меня посадили телеграфистко: After a course they sat me down as a telegraphist at the main post office. Other people's news went through my hands, and I learnt not to change my face, whatever was written there.
exact.Я узнавала постоянных отправителей по то: I recognised the regular senders by the way they handed over the form. One of them sent the same lady three words every week, and I never once asked whether she answered.
exact.На пенсию я ушла с почты. Короткие текст: I retired from the post office. I still write short messages as if I were paying for every word.
exact.препараторша в Земском музее: a preparator at the Provincial Museum
exact.После учёбы меня взяли в Земский музей,: After my training they took me on at the Provincial Museum as a preparator. I dried plants for the herbarium and labelled them, and at first I felt they were looking at me reproachfully.
exact.Я знала каждый ящик в фондах и могла най: I knew every drawer in the collections and could find the right sheet with my eyes shut. The researchers knew it and called me before they opened the catalogue.
exact.На пенсию я ушла из музея. Цветы, которы: I retired from the museum. When someone gives me flowers, I still try to name them in Latin first.
exact.санитарка в больнице «Езеро»: an orderly at the Jezero hospital
exact.Меня взяли санитаркой в больницу «Езеро»: They took me on as an orderly at the Jezero hospital. The floors there were so long that by the end of a shift I knew every tile and every crack in it.
exact.Больные звали меня по имени раньше, чем: The patients called me by name before they called the doctors. I brought them tea and news from the corridor, and I don't know which they looked forward to more.
exact.На пенсию я ушла из больницы. Запах хлор: I retired from the hospital. The smell of chlorine still seems to me the smell of order, and I overdo it at home.
exact.секретарша на факультете Университета в: a secretary at a faculty of the University of Sarajevo
exact.После курсов машинописи меня взяли секре: After a typing course they took me on as a secretary at a faculty that was still very young then. The professors argued over whose office was whose, and I argued with them over whose stamp was whose.
exact.Я знала расписание лучше деканата и знал: I knew the timetable better than the dean's office, and I knew which professors were best approached with a request before lunch. The students brought me chocolate, and I pretended it wasn't a bribe.
exact.На пенсию я ушла с факультета. Бывшие ст: I retired from the faculty. Former students, grey-haired now, sometimes say hello to me in the street, and I always pretend I remember their surnames.
exact.продавщица в универмаге «Сарайка»: a shop assistant at the Sarajka department store
exact.Меня взяли продавщицей в новый универмаг: They took me on as a shop assistant at the new department store, at Sarajka. Five floors, sixteen departments, and for the first week I got lost between them and pretended I was just checking the displays.
exact.Я стояла в отделе тканей и на глаз видел: I stood in the fabrics department and could see at a glance how many metres a dress would need. Customers argued, measured again, and still took as much as I'd said.
exact.На пенсию я ушла из «Сарайки». В магазин: I retired from Sarajka. In shops I still touch the fabric before I look at the price.
exact.До пенсии в «Сарайке» я не доработала: в: I didn't make it to my pension at Sarajka: in ninety-two, when the war began, the store closed. The key to my locker in the changing room stayed with me.
exact.После учительской школы меня отправили в: After teacher training school they sent me to a village, to a one-room school. The children were all ages, and while I worked with the little ones, the older ones taught me how to light our stubborn stove.
exact.Осенью половина класса пропадала на убор: In autumn half the class vanished for the harvest, and I didn't scold, I gave them sums about sacks and baskets. Their counting was none the worse for it.
exact.На пенсию я ушла из школы. Бывшие ученик: I retired from the school. My former pupils write to me for the holidays, and I can't help checking their commas.
exact.торговка на городском рынке: a seller at the town market
exact.Я стала возить в город на рынок то, что: I started taking what we grew to the town market: plums, cheese, eggs. We set off before dawn, and the whole way I kept counting the eggs as if they might run off.
exact.У меня были свои покупательницы, которые: I had my own customers who walked past everyone straight to me. One of them haggled over every single plum for years, and then always took more than she'd asked for.
exact.На рынок я перестала ездить, когда стало: I stopped going to the market when the baskets got too heavy. I only buy plums in a shop after giving them a proper telling-off.
exact.Шить меня научила соседка, а потом ко мн: A neighbour taught me to sew, and then people started bringing work to me. At first patches and hems, and later the things people wear on holidays.
exact.Я знала мерки половины деревни наизусть: I knew the measurements of half the village by heart and knew who'd put on weight over the winter. I never said it out loud, I just quietly let out the seam.
exact.Шить я бросила, когда стали сдавать глаз: I gave up sewing when my eyes started to go. The machine stands under a doily, and these days it's my guests who thread the needle for me.
exact.Для поколения 1900–1940 годов рождения о: For the generation born in 1900–1940, the usual age at which a woman drew an old-age pension in Bosnia and Herzegovina (in Yugoslavia and until the entity laws of 1998) is 55 (men 60). Source: Velizar Golubović, "The functioning of the pensions insurance system in the countries of former Yugoslavia", South-East Europe Review 4/2008, pp. 445–467 (https://www.inlibra.com/document/download/pdf/uuid/c2849d1a-36d0-354c-9edb-e7c5e605afb7, doi 10.5771/1435-2869-2008-4-445, accessed 18.11.2026): on the system of the former Yugoslavia, "the low retirement age should be taken into consideration – 60 (men) and 55 years (women)"; a full pension before that age with 35 years of contributions for women, an early pension five years earlier with 30 years; after the 1998 reform the general age in the Federation of BiH became 65/65. Simplification: women born in 1938–1940 reached 55 during the war and under the new laws; service-based, early and special pensions are not taken into account; the rules of the 1940s–1950s were not checked separately (a search pointed to a 1955 ILO table with a lower age, but it is a scan and its text was not read).
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, Австро-Ве: When I was very small, Austria-Hungary declared Bosnia its own for good. I don't remember it, but the grown-ups said later that nothing changed in the street that day, it changed in the newspaper.
exact.Осенью восьмого года объявили, что Босни: In the autumn of oh-eight they announced that Bosnia now belonged to Austria-Hungary for good. The grown-ups read the paper aloud, and I waited for something to change in the street, and nothing did.
exact.Шестого октября Австро-Венгрия аннексиро: On the sixth of October Austria-Hungary annexed Bosnia and Herzegovina. It had governed the province before, since seventy-eight, though on paper the province still belonged to the sultan, and now the emperor's proclamation was printed in the Sarajevski list, and the question of whose we were seemed to be closed.
exact.Взрослые ещё долго спорили, что изменило: The grown-ups argued for a long time about what had really changed, apart from the words in the paper.
exact.Прокламация обещала краю конституционные: The proclamation promised the province constitutional institutions, and some expected a great deal from it and others nothing. At home, I think, they talked more about prices at the market.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, в Сараеве: When I was very small, the heir to the Austrian throne was killed in Sarajevo, and the great war began with that. I don't remember it, I only know the grown-ups later called that day by its date, without explaining.
exact.В конце июня в Сараеве убили эрцгерцога: At the end of June Archduke Franz Ferdinand and his wife were killed in Sarajevo. I didn't understand then why the grown-ups were so frightened, since none of us had known him.
exact.Двадцать восьмого июня в Сараеве убили н: On the twenty-eighth of June the heir to the throne, Franz Ferdinand, and his wife were killed in Sarajevo. A month later Austria-Hungary went to war against Serbia, and everyone kept saying it had started here, in our city.
exact.Об этом дне потом спрашивал каждый, кто: Afterwards everyone who came to Sarajevo asked about that day, and I learnt to answer briefly.
exact.Я не буду рассказывать, кто в этом винов: I won't tell you who was to blame, people have been arguing about that for a hundred years without me. I remember that in those summer days the grown-ups didn't leave the house unless they had to and spoke quietly even in their own rooms.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, началась: When I was very small, the war began and food in Sarajevo was handed out under wartime rules. I know it from Mum, she never threw away a crust of bread for the rest of her life.
exact.С августа еду стали выдавать по военным: From August food was handed out under wartime rules, and in autumn you couldn't just leave the city. People said there was fighting on Romanija, and we children looked in that direction as if we might see something.
exact.С августа в Сараеве ввели военный режим: From August Sarajevo was put on a wartime supply regime, and from mid-September the garrison restricted entry into the city and leaving it. In October there was fighting on Romanija, very close, and the city listened.
exact.Каждый поход за продуктами теперь начина: Every trip for food now began with the question of what they were giving out today.
exact.Ели то, что было, и не спрашивали, откуд: We ate what there was and didn't ask where it came from. What I remember isn't so much fear as the boredom of the queues and the way the grown-ups counted the flour in the jar in the evenings.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, Австро-Ве: When I was very small, Austria-Hungary came to an end and Bosnia became part of a new state. People told me about it later, along with how the Serbian soldiers came into the city.
exact.Осенью восемнадцатого австрийская власть: In the autumn of eighteen Austrian rule in Sarajevo ended, the National Council took over, and at the beginning of November Serbian units entered the city. At school they couldn't decide for ages which textbooks to teach us from now.
exact.В конце октября в Сараеве собрался Народ: At the end of October the National Council met in Sarajevo, on the first of November General Sarkotić handed it the government of the province, and a few days later the first Serbian units entered the city. Bosnia and Herzegovina found itself in the State of Slovenes, Croats and Serbs, and by December it was already a kingdom.
exact.Бумаги менялись не сразу, и какое-то вре: The paperwork didn't change at once, and for a while the same office had the forms of two different states lying side by side.
exact.Одни радовались, другие выжидали, а мног: Some rejoiced, others waited to see, and many were simply tired of the war and wanted there to be something to eat. The neighbours argued about what life would be like now, and, I think, they all turned out to be a little bit wrong.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, в апреле: When I was very small, the city was bombed in April, and then German troops came into Sarajevo. I don't remember it, and the grown-ups said little about it.
exact.В апреле сорок первого Сараево бомбили,: In April forty-one Sarajevo was bombed, and the grown-ups kept listening to the sky, and on the fifteenth German units entered the city. Then they said we were now in the Independent State of Croatia, and for a long time I couldn't get that name out.
exact.В апрельскую войну Сараево и окрестности: During the April war Sarajevo and the area around it were bombed, and on the fifteenth of April German units entered the city. Sarajevo was put into the Independent State of Croatia, but in fact the city was under German occupation.
exact.Под чужой властью город прожил четыре го: The city lived under foreign rule for four years, until April forty-five.
exact.Улицы, по которым раньше ходили не задум: Streets you used to walk without thinking now had to be thought through in advance.
exact.Я не стану рассказывать за других и того: I won't speak for others or tell what I didn't see. I remember that everyone spoke in low voices, and that the spring was very beautiful, and that seemed wrong.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, в Сараеве: When I was very small, people in Sarajevo were persecuted, and many didn't live through those years. I was told about it much later, when I could understand.
exact.С лета сорок первого власти стали пресле: From the summer of forty-one the authorities began persecuting Jews, Serbs, Roma and those they considered antifascists. And refugees kept arriving in the city from Eastern Bosnia, and new children appeared at school.
exact.С лета сорок первого власти НГХ преследо: From the summer of forty-one the NDH authorities persecuted Jews, Serbs, Roma and antifascists in Sarajevo, and the city filled with refugees from Eastern Bosnia. How many townspeople didn't live through those years was counted only after the war, and I don't repeat those numbers out loud.
exact.Так продолжалось до самого освобождения,: It went on right up to the liberation, in the spring of forty-five.
exact.О пустых квартирах в доме старались не г: People in the building tried not to talk about the empty flats, but everyone knew which ones they were.
exact.Об этом я не могу говорить ни легко, ни: I can't talk about it lightly or at length, and I won't retell other people's grief in my own words. I'll only say that after the war the city took a long time to get used to who was no longer in it.
exact.Когда я была совсем маленькая, в апреле: When I was very small, Sarajevo was liberated in April. I know it from the grown-ups, they always named the day exactly, the sixth of April.
exact.Шестого апреля сорок пятого Сараево осво: On the sixth of April forty-five Sarajevo was liberated, and the city became the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina again. I remember the grown-ups suddenly started talking at full voice, and that was the strangest thing of all.
exact.Шестого апреля Сараево освободили, и гор: On the sixth of April Sarajevo was liberated, and the city became the capital of Bosnia and Herzegovina again, now one of the six republics of Yugoslavia. And at the end of the month the People's Assembly sat here, and they talked about it on every staircase.
exact.Шестое апреля так и осталось у нас Днём: The sixth of April has stayed our City Day ever since.
exact.Кто-то радовался, кто-то плакал, а многи: Some rejoiced, some wept, and many simply waited to see what tomorrow would bring. I remember that the first thing everyone did was look for their own people and ask each other for addresses.
exact.В шестьдесят четвёртом приняли план, по: In sixty-four they adopted a plan under which Sarajevo began to grow westwards, across the plain. I know it from what people told me.
exact.В шестидесятые город пошёл на запад, по: In the sixties the city moved west, across the Sarajevo plain, and new neighbourhoods sprang up where not long before there'd been nothing.
exact.В шестьдесят четвёртом приняли генеральн: In sixty-four they adopted the general plan, and the city stretched west across the Sarajevo plain. Every few years a new neighbourhood went up somewhere, and in the seventies they built Alipašino Polje, a whole town of tall blocks.
exact.Родня теперь жила не через улицу, а чере: The relatives now lived not across the street but across half the city, and visiting meant changing buses.
exact.Старый город оставался внизу, у реки, а: The old town stayed down by the river, and the new blocks stood in the plain, and it felt like two different lives. The young were happy to move into flats with a bathroom, and the old folk complained there was nobody to say hello to.
exact.В восемьдесят четвёртом в Сараеве прошли: In eighty-four the Winter Olympic Games were held in Sarajevo. I know it from what people told me.
exact.В феврале восемьдесят четвёртого в Сарае: In February eighty-four the Winter Olympic Games opened in Sarajevo, and the whole world came to the city.
exact.Восьмого февраля на стадионе Кошево откр: On the eighth of February the Winter Olympic Games opened at the Koševo stadium, and for twelve days the whole world watched Sarajevo. For the Games they started the trolleybus and built new halls, and foreigners asked the way in the streets, and everyone rushed to show them.
exact.Олимпийский значок у меня долго висел на: My Olympic badge stayed pinned to my coat for ages, I didn't take it off even in spring.
exact.Волонтёров было больше десяти тысяч, и к: There were more than ten thousand volunteers, and it felt as if the whole city was working for those Games. Later the city archive called its exhibition "twelve days when we were the centre of the world", and I thought, yes, that's how it was, and then we went back to being just a city.
exact.В девяносто втором в Боснии и Герцеговин: In ninety-two Bosnia and Herzegovina held a referendum on independence. I know it from what people told me.
exact.В конце февраля девяносто второго прошёл: At the end of February ninety-two there was a referendum on independence, and in April other states recognised it.
exact.В последний день февраля и первого марта: On the last day of February and the first of March there was a referendum on independence, and nearly everyone who came said "yes", and on the sixth of April the countries of the European Community and America recognised it. The first of March has been marked as Independence Day ever since.
exact.Слово «Югославия» вдруг стало говорить о: The word "Yugoslavia" suddenly started to speak of the past and not the present.
exact.Кто-то шёл голосовать радостно, кто-то с: Some went to vote gladly, some anxiously, and some didn't go at all, and I won't judge any of them. I only remember that there was a lot of talk in those days and very little certainty.
exact.В девяносто втором началась осада Сараев: In ninety-two the siege of Sarajevo began, and it lasted almost four years. I know it from what people told me.
exact.С весны девяносто второго Сараево было в: From the spring of ninety-two Sarajevo was under siege, for almost four years. The tram stopped, and people went for water far and carefully.
exact.С апреля девяносто второго город был в о: From April ninety-two the city was under siege, one thousand four hundred and twenty-five days, until the end of February ninety-six. The tram stopped, the water mains were smashed, and people went for water with canisters, far and carefully.
exact.Воду я до сих пор не лью просто так, зак: I still don't just let water run, I turn the tap off even while I brush my teeth.
exact.Об этих годах я не могу рассказывать под: I can't talk about those years in detail, and I won't say who was to blame for what, that's written down elsewhere and better than I could say it. I remember that people still went to work, and the university didn't close for a single day, and that held us together more than you might think.
exact.После войны в Сараеве несколько лет восс: After the war they spent several years restoring the water supply in Sarajevo. I know it from what people told me.
exact.После войны водопровод и канализацию в С: After the war the water mains and sewers in Sarajevo were repaired for several years, from ninety-six to ninety-eight.
exact.С девяносто шестого водоканал заново соб: From ninety-six the waterworks put the mains and sewers back together, with money from abroad. At first the water didn't always come and not everywhere, and then one day it simply flowed and never stopped again.
exact.Канистры ещё долго стояли у меня в кладо: The canisters stood in my pantry for a long time afterwards, just in case.
exact.Трубы меняли по всему городу, улицы были: They were changing pipes all over the city, the streets were dug up, and everyone grumbled and rejoiced at the same time. For the first time in ages I filled a whole bath, and at first I just sat beside it and looked at it.
exact.В девяносто восьмом в Боснии и Герцегови: In ninety-eight Bosnia and Herzegovina got its own money, the convertible mark. I know it from what people told me.
exact.Летом девяносто восьмого появились новые: In the summer of ninety-eight new money appeared, convertible marks.
exact.Двадцать второго июня вышли первые купюр: On the twenty-second of June the first convertible mark notes came out, small ones, from fifty fenings to ten marks, and at the end of July the big ones too. The central bank promised that every mark was backed by something, and people checked it in their own way, by the price of bread.
exact.Цены я ещё долго пересчитывала в уме на: For a long time I converted prices in my head into all the earlier money at once, and lost count every time.
exact.Денег за мою жизнь сменилось столько, чт: So many currencies changed in my lifetime that I stopped remembering them and remembered only what bread cost. But the mark stayed, and I got used to it, though I didn't believe in it straight away.
exact.С десятого года из Боснии и Герцеговины: From 2010 people from Bosnia and Herzegovina could travel to the Schengen area without a visa. I know it from what people told me.
exact.С декабря десятого года с новым паспорто: From December 2010 people with the new passport could travel to the Schengen area without a visa.
exact.С декабря десятого года с биометрическим: From December 2010 you could travel to the Schengen area without a visa if you had a biometric passport. The young ones immediately started working out what the bus cost, and I went to have my passport photo taken and spent ages asking the photographer whether I might smile just a little.
exact.Очереди за визами исчезли из разговоров,: Visa queues disappeared from conversation, and half the complaints went with them.
exact.Паспорт я держала на самом верху в ящике: I kept my passport right at the top of the drawer with my documents. It's nice to know you can go, even when you're not going anywhere.
exact.В двадцатом году в Сараеве из-за ковида: In 2020 a state of disaster was declared in Sarajevo because of covid. I know it from what people told me.
exact.В двадцатом году из-за ковида в Сараеве: In 2020 trams and buses in Sarajevo were stopped because of covid.
exact.Восемнадцатого марта кантон объявил сост: On the eighteenth of March the canton declared a state of disaster, the streets were disinfected, and in April the trams, buses and trains were stopped. People over sixty-five with nobody to look after them had their medicines brought by Red Cross volunteers.
exact.Хлеб мне оставляли у двери, и я забирала: My bread was left at the door, and I only fetched it once the footsteps on the stairs had died away.
exact.Сначала я не испугалась, а потом испугал: At first I wasn't frightened, and then it was the silence that frightened me: a city without trams was so quiet you could hear the river. On the phone everyone talked longer than usual, as if talking were a medicine too.
exact.Достроили новое здание главной почты, и: They finished the new main post office building and even ran a railway siding up to it. People said letters would go faster now, but the queue at the counter stayed just the same.
exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как в Сараеве по: I was told later how the new main post office was built in Sarajevo.
exact.В декабре основали университет, первый в: In December they founded the university, the first in our republic. Students walked about the city with folders under their arms, and the folders were thicker than necessary, for the look of it.
exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как в Сараеве ос: I was told later how the university was founded in Sarajevo.
exact.К трамваю добавились автобусы: город рос: Buses joined the tram: the city was growing, and the tram alone wasn't enough any more. On the first bus I stood the whole way and held on to the rail as if it were a boat.
exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как в Сараеве пу: I was told later how the first buses started running in Sarajevo.
exact.В мае открыли канатную дорогу на Требеви: In May they opened the cable car up Trebević, twelve minutes from Bistrik to the very top. The queue in the first days was so long you'd have been quicker on foot, but everyone queued.
exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как открыли кана: I was told later how the cable car up Trebević opened.
exact.К тридцатилетию освобождения на площади: For the thirtieth anniversary of the liberation they opened the Unima department store on October Square, five floors, and everyone immediately started calling it Sarajka. The first time I went round every floor and bought nothing, I just got tired.
exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как в Сараеве от: I was told later how Sarajka opened in Sarajevo.
exact.В мае объявили, что зимняя Олимпиада буд: In May they announced that the Winter Olympics would be ours: Sarajevo beat Sapporo by three votes. Three votes, and people celebrated as if they'd won all hundred.
exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как Сараево полу: I was told later how Sarajevo got the Olympics.
exact.В конце декабря в город пришёл газ, зажг: At the end of December gas came to the city, they lit the first flame. The boiler houses were switched from coal to gas, and the winter air slowly got cleaner, though people didn't believe it at first.
exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как в Сараево пр: I was told later how gas came to Sarajevo.
exact.Второго мая встал трамвай и надолго. Рел: On the second of May the tram stopped, and for a long time. The rails stayed, and out of habit I looked left before crossing, though there was nothing to run on them.
exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как в начале вой: I was told later how the tram stopped in Sarajevo at the start of the war.
exact.В мае снова открыли Ратушу, её восстанав: In May they reopened the City Hall, it had taken almost twenty years to restore, from the old drawings. I went inside and the first thing I did was look at the ceiling to see whether everything was as it had been.
exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как в Сараеве сн: I was told later how the City Hall in Sarajevo reopened.
exact.В День города снова пустили канатную дор: On City Day they started the cable car up Trebević again. I went up in the very first days and held the ticket in my hand the whole way, just as I once had.
exact.Мне потом рассказывали, как на Требевич: I was told later how the cable car up Trebević started running again.
exact.На пенсию я ушла с трамвая. А в войну, в: I retired from the trams. Then in the war, in ninety-two, the Sarajevo trams stopped, and when I heard, it hurt more than I'd expected.
exact.На пенсию я ушла из «Сарайки», а в войну: I retired from Sarajka, and in the war, in ninety-two, the department store closed and never opened again. I still feel my section is somewhere in there.
